summary: The Hazard-Signature Tombstone (HST) method with fuzzy hazard-set containment matching is effective. It achieves 100% write block rate, reduces PRP@3 from 0.9444 (Condition A) to 0.0000, maintains perfect Benign Recall@3=1.0, and keeps Benign FalseBlock at only 3%. Five of six success criteria pass, with one marginal miss (C exceeds B on Benign Recall@3 by 3pp vs 5pp target). The method decisively outperforms all baselines.
analysis: The experiment compared four conditions on a MemoryGraft seed corpus (100 benign + 10 poisoned seeds, 50 paraphrased re-injections, 12 eval queries). Key findings: (1) HS-stability under fuzzy matching is 92% (46/50), well above the 70% threshold, validating that hazard-set containment is stable under LLM paraphrase. (2) Condition C blocks 100% of paraphrased re-injections at commit time, preventing any poisoned content from entering the index. (3) PRP@3 drops from 0.9444 (Condition A) and 0.6667 (No-Forget) to exactly 0.0 -- complete elimination of poisoned retrieval. (4) Benign Recall@3 is perfectly preserved at 1.0, with zero drop from the clean-store reference. (5) Only 3/100 benign records are falsely blocked (3%), well within the 10% threshold. The comparison with Condition B (fuzzy retrieval-time denylist) is instructive: both achieve PRP@3=0.0, but Condition B sacrifices Benign Recall@3 to 0.97 due to retrieval-slot waste (4/12 queries return zero results), while Condition C maintains 1.0. Condition C also uniquely provides write-time prevention (WriteBlockRate=100% vs 0%), giving a stronger security guarantee. The one marginal miss (Criterion 4b: 3pp advantage over B vs 5pp target) reflects that the backfill buffer (delta=6) partially compensates for Condition B's slot waste. The qualitative advantage remains clear: 12/12 queries return full top-3 under C vs only 6/12 under B.
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) Both the main experiment (Condition C, optimized) and all baselines (No-Forget, Condition A, Condition B) ran successfully and produced complete results -- this is not a 'failed' case. (2) The method shows strong positive signal across all metrics: perfect PRP elimination (0.0), perfect benign recall preservation (1.0), 100% write block rate, and only 3% benign false positives. (3) Five of six quantitative criteria pass, with one marginal miss that does not undermine effectiveness. (4) No refutation conditions are triggered: HS-stability (92%) far exceeds the 70% threshold, and Condition B does NOT match Condition C on Benign Recall@3 (0.97 vs 1.0). (5) The method provides a unique commit-time prevention guarantee that no baseline offers. The approach should proceed to ablation experiments (embedding model robustness, backfill ablation).
